title: Making the Path Shorter and Smoother: Shortcuts Between Random Points, Corners Cut Where There Is Room, and the Clearance Both Quietly Spend

questions.question: What is a shortcut?
options: Removing every vertex that is closer than the margin
Replacing the whole path by the line from start to goal
Replacing the part of a path between two random points by the straight edge, if it is free
Running the planner again with a smaller step
questions.explanation: Two points are picked at random along the path. If the straight edge between them is free, everything between them is thrown away.

questions.question: The path was how many times the straight line before and after shortcutting?
options: 4.83 then 1.00, the straight line
4.83 then 4.83: only the corners changed
questions.explanation: 150 tries took most of the wandering out. It cannot reach 1.00 here, because the straight line goes through the wall.

questions.question: The sharpest turn went from 2.25 rad to:
options: 0.00 rad: a straight path
2.25 rad, unchanged, since corners are vertices
1.85 rad
0.60 rad after cutting the corners twice
questions.explanation: Each round replaces a vertex by two points and one checked edge, which blunts the turn. Two rounds brought the sharpest from 2.25 to 0.60 rad.

questions.question: The clearance along the path after shortcutting with no margin and with the margin kept was:
options: 0.02 and 0.02 m: the planner's margin is kept either way
questions.explanation: A smoother that checks with no margin will hug an obstacle to a tenth of a millimetre. Given the planner's 0.02 m, it kept 0.0202 m.

questions.question: Why must a corner cut be checked only for the middle edge?
options: The outer pieces are too short to hit anything
The two outer pieces lie on the old segments, which were free
The middle edge is the only one near an obstacle
Checking all three would take three times as long
questions.explanation: The new points sit on the old segments, so the pieces up to them are parts of edges already known to be free. Only the edge across the corner is new.

questions.question: Why are random shortcuts a good first pass?
options: They find the shortest path there is
They need no collision checks
They never move the path closer to obstacles
A random path is full of detours that a straight edge skips, and a hundred tries find most
questions.explanation: A tree's path doubles back in many places. Almost any pair of points either side of a detour gives a free straight edge that removes it.
